%% Hand-authored circuitikz figure -- NOT generated by maestro2tex.
%% Topology transcribed from the anatop_biasgen_local netlist.
\begin{figure}[htbp]
  \centering
  \resizebox{0.82\linewidth}{!}{%
\ctikzset{bipoles/length=0.9cm, transistors/scale=0.82}
\begin{circuitikz}[
    every node/.append style={font=\footnotesize},
    gatelab/.style={font=\scriptsize, inner sep=1pt},
    railnode/.style={circle, fill=black, inner sep=1.05pt},
  ]
\def\yvdd{5.7} \def\yvss{0.2} \def\yrow{1.7}
\draw[thick] (-1.7,\yvdd) -- (8.9,\yvdd) node[right]{$V_{\mathrm{DD}}$};
\draw[thick] (-1.7,\yvss) -- (8.9,\yvss) node[right]{$V_{\mathrm{SS}}$};

% --- weak always-on pull-up generates V_SU ---
\node[pmos](P1) at (0,4.2){};
\draw (P1.source) -- (0,\yvdd);
\node[gatelab, left] at (P1.gate){$V_{\mathrm{SS}}$};
\draw (P1.drain) -- (0,3.0);
\node[railnode] at (0,3.0){};
\node[gatelab, right=3pt, yshift=6pt] at (0,3.0){$V_{\mathrm{SU}}$};

% --- M0 collapses V_SU once the core is running ---
\node[nmos](N0) at (0,\yrow){};
\draw (N0.drain) -- (0,3.0);
\draw (N0.source) -- (0,\yvss);
\node[gatelab, left] at (N0.gate){$V_{\mathrm{BNC}}$};

% --- M12 holds V_SU low while the cell is disabled ---
\node[nmos](N12) at (2.2,\yrow){};
\draw (N12.drain) -- (2.2,3.0) -- (0,3.0);
\draw (N12.source) -- (2.2,\yvss);
\node[gatelab, left] at (N12.gate){$\overline{\mathrm{En}}$};

% --- the two kick devices ---
\node[nmos](N3) at (5.4,\yrow){};
\draw (N3.source) -- (5.4,\yvss);
\draw (N3.drain) -- (5.4,4.3) node[above, font=\scriptsize]{$\rightarrow V_{\mathrm{BPM}}$};
\node[gatelab, left] at (N3.gate){$V_{\mathrm{SU}}$};

\node[nmos](N2) at (7.8,\yrow){};
\draw (N2.source) -- (7.8,\yvss);
\draw (N2.drain) -- (7.8,4.3) node[above, font=\scriptsize]{$\rightarrow V_{\mathrm{BPC}}$};
\node[gatelab, left] at (N2.gate){$V_{\mathrm{SU}}$};
\end{circuitikz}
  }
  \caption[{Start-up branch of the local bias generator.}]{Start-up branch. A gate-grounded, permanently-on weak PMOS pulls $V_{\mathrm{SU}}$ up at power-on; while $V_{\mathrm{SU}}$ is high it drags $V_{\mathrm{BPM}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{BPC}}$ down, forcing current into the core and breaking the degenerate zero-current state. Once the core is running, the rising $V_{\mathrm{BNC}}$ turns on the left NMOS and collapses $V_{\mathrm{SU}}$, so the branch draws no static current in normal operation --- the behaviour visible in the power-up transient of Figure~\ref{fig:biasgen-startup}. A second device holds $V_{\mathrm{SU}}$ low whenever the cell is disabled.}
  \label{fig:biasgen-startup-sch}
\end{figure}
